mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.0% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their prior six-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 6-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 6-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) combined with a flat or declining housing starts index (HOUST) suggests a shift from durable goods to services consumption, which historically correlates with lower capital expenditure and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >0.5% MoM and HOUST does not rise MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS rises >0.5% MoM and HOUST is flat or declines.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals increased labor supply without corresponding wage growth, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable and PAYEMS rises for three consecutive months
regime_hint: labor supply expansion without wage growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative under the described labor supply expansion regime.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS rising faster than GDPC1) for four consecutive months signals a buildup of precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS grows faster than GDPC1 for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS outpaces GDPC1 growth for four months.
